title: Early machines & the factory system
intro: Spinning jennies, water frames and steam engines. Arkwright builds the first great mills at Cromford; Boulton and Watt sell power by the horse.

title: War, hunger & the Luddites
intro: War with France closes markets and raises the price of bread. In Nottinghamshire, Yorkshire and Lancashire, workers break the machines they blame, and Parliament makes frame-breaking a capital crime.

title: Peterloo & unrest
intro: A peaceful reform meeting at St Peter's Field, Manchester, is charged by yeomanry. An economist publicly changes his mind about machinery.

title: The railway age begins
intro: Stockton & Darlington, the Rainhill Trials, and the opening of the Liverpool & Manchester Railway, with its first famous casualty. Poets and reviewers argue over whether any of this is progress.

title: Factories under scrutiny
intro: Carlyle names the Mechanical Age. Oastler compares the mills to slavery, Sadler's Committee takes evidence from factory children, and the Factory Act of 1833 is passed.

title: Chartism & the hungry forties
intro: The People's Charter, mass petitions, strikes and depression. Novelists, poets and a young German clerk describe the condition of England.

title: The Great Exhibition
intro: A palace of glass in Hyde Park displays the works of industry of all nations. Six million visits; on shilling days, the working people come to look at the machines.

title: Afterword: the 1850s
intro: Looking back on the age. Coketown, the division of men, and the gospel of self-help.
